name: orca
description: Orca is the place for working with a fleet of agents (e.g. Grok Bot, Claude Code). Run any coding agent with your own subscription. Available on desktop, mobile and remote runtime.
readmeExcerpt:
Orca

中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Español · Français · Português · Türkçe · Русский

The AI Orchestrator for 100x builders.
Run Codex, ClaudeCode, OpenCode or Pi side-by-side — each in its own worktree, tracked in one place.

Download Orca

## Features
### Mobile Companion Monitor and steer your agents from your phone — get notified when an agent finishes and send follow-ups from anywhere. [iOS App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/orca-ide/id6766130217) · [Android APK](https://www.onorca.dev/download/android) · [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/mobile)
### Parallel Worktrees Fan one prompt across five agents, each in its own isolated git worktree — compare the results and merge the winner. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/model/worktrees)
### Terminal Splits Ghostty-class terminals with WebGL rendering, infinite splits, and scrollback that survives restarts. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/terminal)
### Design Mode Click any UI element in a real Chromium window to send its HTML, CSS, and a cropped screenshot straight into your agent's prompt. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/browser/design-mode)
### GitHub & Linear, Native Browse PRs, issues, and project boards in-app — open a worktree from any task and review without a context switch. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/review/linear)
### SSH Worktrees Run agents on a beefy remote box with full file editing, git, and terminals — auto-reconnect and port forwarding included. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/ssh)
### Annotate AI Diffs Drop comments on any diff line and ship them back to the agent — review, edit, and commit without leaving Orca. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/review/annotate-ai-diff)
### Drag Files to Agents VS Code's editor with autosave everywhere — drag files or images straight into an agent prompt. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/editing/file-explorer)
### Orca CLI Agents drive Orca too — script every workflow with `orca worktree create`, `snapshot`, `click`, and `fill`. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/cli/overview)
**Also in the box:** - **[Quick open](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/model/quick-open)** — Search across worktrees, files, agents, commands, and repo context without leaving your flow. - **[Account switcher & usage tracking](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/agents/usage-tracking)** — See Claude and Codex usage and rate-limit resets, and hot-swap accounts without re-logging in. - **[Rich repo previews](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/editing/markdown)** — Preview Markdown, images, PDFs, and repo docs in the workspace. - **[Computer Use](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/cli/computer-use)** — Let agents operate desktop apps and visible UI when a workflow needs real interaction. - **[Notifications and unread state](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/notifications)** — Know when an agent finishes or needs attention, then mark threads unread to come back later. - **And many, many more** — we ship daily, so this list is perpetually behind. The [changelog](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases) is the real feature list. --- ## Supported Agents Works with **any CLI agent** — if it runs in a terminal, it runs in Orca.

Claude Code   Codex   Grok   Cursor   GitHub Copilot   Muse   DeepSeek Harness   ZCode   OpenCode   MiMo Code   Amp   OpenClaude   Antigravity   Pi   oh-my-pi   Hermes Agent   Devin   Goose   Auggie   Autohand Code

aiSummary.oneLiner: An AI orchestrator enabling developers to run multiple autonomous coding agents simultaneously in parallel worktrees.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Orca functions as a sophisticated Agent Development Environment (ADE) designed specifically to orchestrate fleets of parallel AI coding agents. It wraps multiple independent sessions, allowing users to concurrently run models like Claude Code, Codex, or Pi within their own isolated git worktrees. Available seamlessly across native desktop, mobile, and VPS environments, Orca centralizes task management and provides extremely fast, WebGL-rendered Ghostty-class terminals to monitor output. It effectively multiplies a single developer's bandwidth by allowing them to supervise and steer multiple autonomous refactoring or development tasks simultaneously.
keyFeatures: Parallel orchestration: Expertly manages multiple autonomous coding agents running simultaneously in completely isolated git worktrees.
Cross-platform support: Provides native applications for desktop environments, mobile devices, and remote headless Linux servers.
High-performance terminals: Includes extremely fast, WebGL-rendered terminals with highly persistent scrollback for monitoring agent output.
Mobile supervision: Includes a dedicated mobile companion app to actively monitor agent progress and send follow-up commands remotely.
Subscription flexibility: Allows users to easily integrate their own provider API keys to directly manage inference costs across the fleet.

useCases.title: Massive refactoring
useCases.description: Deploy a swarm of specialized agents to concurrently update syntax across hundreds of files in a large repository.

useCases.title: Remote supervision
useCases.description: Developers start a complex, long-running agent task on their desktop and monitor its progress from their phone during a commute.

useCases.title: Distributed testing
useCases.description: QA leads spin up parallel agents in isolated worktrees to simultaneously write and execute test suites against different microservices.

useCases.title: Cost optimization
useCases.description: Power users utilize custom API keys within the orchestrator to heavily manage and optimize the financial cost of running multiple agents.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Power users, tech leads, and highly ambitious developers aiming to drastically scale their output by orchestrating multi-agent workflows. It is ideal for teams comfortable managing complex, distributed development environments.

## Chrome extensions in Orca’s browser, iPhone Duo support, and Convert a terminal agent session live into a chat ui 🧩

This release brings Chrome extensions to Orca’s browser under experimental, lets a conversation continue in Chat once you quit its agent in the terminal, and shows your local worktrees sooner after a restart. It also adds support for the folding iPhone Duo, compact native-style menus, light and dark themes on the phone, and fixes for Windows terminals, SSH hosts and updates.

## The short version

- **Chrome extensions (experimental):** Add extensions from the Chrome Web Store with **Add to Orca**, so password managers like Bitwarden and 1Password can fill logins in Orca’s browser. Off by default.
- **Convert a terminal agent session live into a chat ui:** Once you quit Claude or Codex in a terminal, the same conversation can continue in Chat while the terminal tab stays open. Claude chats also keep their saved approval choice across model changes, and closing a chat that’s still working asks first.

## Lighter on memory, Claude subagents a click away, and remote servers that remember 🪄

This release is lighter on memory, with lower memory use in the terminal host and WSL connections, plus less idle CPU use in terminals. It also lets you open Claude subagents straight from the sidebar, makes Codex chats in Ask mode ask before editing, and helps paired servers, SSH and WSL hosts keep your tabs and explain failures. This release also fixes problems across Windows, Linux and macOS.

## The short version

- **Open Claude subagents from the sidebar:** Click a Claude subagent row in the sidebar or dashboard to open its transcript in the same terminal, then click the parent to go back. An eye marks the one you’re viewing.
- **Chats that ask first:** Codex chats in Ask mode now ask before editing your workspace, remote Claude terminals on paired servers can continue in Chat, and chats that can’t start tell you why.
- **Agents resume as you left them:** Resumed Claude sessions keep their effort level and launch flags, Codex keeps the permission you last gave it, and Session History finds chats in more folders and on servers.

## Chats and a browser that behave the way you expect 🧭

This release makes chats follow your agent settings, brings Chrome-style tools to the built-in browser, and helps SSH connections and managed servers recover. You’ll also find a chat font setting, live agent browsing, and steadier Hermes, Kimi, Kiro and Windows terminals.

## The short version

- **Chats that follow your settings:** New chats use each agent’s permission from Settings → Agents, renamed chats keep their names in Session History, and a chat won’t write a conversation a terminal is still running.
- **A browser closer to Chrome:** Dock DevTools inside the pane, mute tabs playing sound, see a link’s URL on hover, and use Orca shortcuts and mouse back/forward inside pages.
- **Watch agents browse:** A cursor and badge show where an agent is clicking or typing, chat jumps you to the page, and links from terminals and chat open beside their source.
- **SSH with fewer dead ends:** Saved port forwards return after a restart and explain failures, certificate-only hosts connect through your system `ssh`, and managed servers update without closing terminals.

releases.name: Orca Mobile Android mobile-android-v0.0.59
releases.body:
Thank you for using Orca mobile! ❤️

## What's new

- Opening Orca after your computer updates is about twice as fast. Downloads are decoded faster, and only the files that changed are fetched instead of the whole app.
- The download progress bar now fills smoothly instead of jumping to the end.
- Going back to a screen you already have open takes you there instead of opening another copy.
- Terminal output that the phone sometimes dropped, such as the screen reset after a full-screen program exits, now shows up.

Most phone features come from your desktop, so update Orca on your computer to get everything. See the [desktop release notes](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases) for the full list.

### Verify your download

- Size: `136281689` bytes
- SHA-256: `f8a18086b04dc00966431edc4d484132d6fc8dc08a5d88009a3246317a12f343`

A "no certificate" or "problem parsing the package" install failure is usually a truncated download — check the size first, then `sha256sum -c app-release.apk.sha256` (`shasum -a 256 -c` on macOS).

releases.body:
## A more dependable workspace 🐳

This release gives the built-in browser searchable history, makes agent activity easier to follow, and improves recovery across chats and remote terminals. You’ll also find Lean and Zig syntax highlighting, support for larger quick-command collections, and a new `orca ports` command for finding your dev servers.

## The short version

- **Conversations that stay with you:** Claude chats now show turns made outside Orca. Retained messages return after reconnect without reopening the chat, and crash recovery no longer guesses that a sent message was undelivered.
- **A browser with a better memory:** Search your browsing history, reopen pages, remove unwanted suggestions, and clear history with Undo. Pages can also use files you pick, save or drop through File System Access.
- **Remote work with fewer interruptions:** Slow connections survive missed wake probes, reconnect notices explain what is happening, SSH terminals wait for sign-in, and new splits stay on the paired server.

Docs →

Also in the box:

  • Quick open — Search across worktrees, files, agents, commands, and repo context without leaving your flow.
  • Account switcher & usage tracking — See Claude and Codex usage and rate-limit resets, and hot-swap accounts without re-logging in.
  • Rich repo previews — Preview Markdown, images, PDFs, and repo docs in the workspace.
  • Computer Use — Let agents operate desktop apps and visible UI when a workflow needs real interaction.
  • Notifications and unread state — Know when an agent finishes or needs attention, then mark threads unread to come back later.
  • And many, many more — we ship daily, so this list is perpetually behind. The changelog is the real feature list.

Supported Agents

Works with any CLI agent — if it runs in a terminal, it runs in Orca.

Claude Code   Codex   Grok   Cursor   GitHub Copilot   Muse   DeepSeek Harness   ZCode   OpenCode   MiMo Code   Amp   OpenClaude   Antigravity   Pi   oh-my-pi   Hermes Agent   Devin   Goose   Auggie   Autohand Code   Charm   Cline   CodeBuddy   Codebuff   Freebuff   Command Code   Continue   Droid   Kilocode   Kimi   Kiro   Mistral Vibe   Qwen Code   Rovo Dev   + any CLI agent

Install

Desktop — macOS, Windows, Linux

  • Download from onOrca.dev
  • Or grab a build directly: macOS Apple Silicon · macOS Intel · Windows (.exe) · Linux AppImage · All builds

Or via a package manager:

# macOS (Homebrew)
# Always use the full name; bare `orca` is an unrelated Plotly cask.
brew install --cask stablyai/orca/orca
# Upgrade an existing install
brew upgrade --cask stablyai/orca/orca

# Arch Linux (AUR) — or stably-orca-git to build from source
yay -S stably-orca-bin

Mobile Companion — iOS, Android

Pair with your desktop app to monitor and steer your agents from your phone.

  • iOS: Download on the App Store
  • Android: Download APK · Install guide

Community & Support

  • Discord: Join the community on Discord.

  • Twitter / X: Follow @orca_build for updates and announcements.

  • WeChat: Group 12 is full. Scan to join the Orca community WeChat group 13.

  • Feedback & Ideas: We ship fast. Missing something? Request a new feature.

  • Privacy: See the privacy & telemetry docs for what anonymous usage data Orca collects and how to opt out.

  • Show Support: Star this repo to follow along with our daily ships.

Developing

Want to contribute or run locally? See our CONTRIBUTING.md guide.

The relay that pairs the mobile app with a desktop host is also in this repository under cloud/, with a separate pnpm workspace and setup guide.

Signed Builds

Windows code signing sponsored/provided by SignPath.io, certificate by SignPath Foundation.

License

Orca is free and open source under the MIT License.
